paper.title: Offline Clustering of Linear Bandits: The Power of Clusters under Limited Data

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline policy learning from a fixed logged dataset (single decision for a test user); not an interactive bandit problem.
unmapped: U users partitioned into J unknown clusters sharing preference vectors; minimum inter-cluster gap gamma (heterogeneity gap)
Fixed offline dataset with N_u samples per user; objective is suboptimality gap for a test user on an arbitrary test action set

Action regularity: offline actions chosen from finite candidate sets of size <= S drawn i.i.d. from rho with min eigenvalue lambda_a; the learner knows the smoothed regularity parameter tilde lambda_a
The learner knows the number of users U
settings.definition_quote: In the offline setting, we are given a dataset $\mathcal{D} = \{\mathcal{D}_1, \cdots, \mathcal{D}_U\}$ comprising offline samples collected from $U$ users. ... $R(\bm{a}_u^i)$ is a 1-subgaussian reward distribution ... SubOpt(u_test,pi,A_test) := <theta_{u_test}, a*_test> - <theta_{u_test}, a_{pi(u_test)}>

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Offline policy learning from a fixed logged dataset; not an interactive bandit problem.
unmapped: U users partitioned into unknown clusters; fixed offline dataset; suboptimality for a test user
settings.definition_quote:
Given any test user $u_{\textnormal{test}} \in \mathcal{U}$, consider the set of \oclub{} instances: $
\mathcal{I}_{u_{\textnormal{test}}} = \big\{ (\mathcal{D}, \Theta, R) \,\big|\, \big\|\left( M^{\mathcal{V}(j_{u_{\textnormal{test}}})} \right)^{-\frac{1}{2}} \bm{a}_{\textnormal{test}}^* \big\|_2 \leq 2\sqrt{2},\; R \textnormal{ is 1-subgaussian} \big\}$

symbols.N_V: total samples of the test user and its neighbours in graph G_gamma_hat
symbols.eta_W: fraction of (regularised) samples from heterogeneous neighbours

conditions: lambda <= d log(1+min_u N_u/(lambda d)) + 2 log(2U/delta)

results.notes: Suboptimality gap of one offline decision mapped to simple_regret; probability 1-2delta.

symbols.N_V_gamma: total samples of the test user and its neighbours in graph G_gamma

tuning: gamma_hat = gamma (requires knowing the heterogeneity gap gamma)

source.label: corollary_gamma_known
source.quote: With the same notations as \Cref{th2}, if \(\hat\gamma = \gamma\) in Algorithm \ref{al2}, the suboptimality gap satisfies: SubOpt <= \tilde O( sqrt(d/(tilde lambda_a N_{V_gamma(u_test)})) ).

results.notes: Requires gamma known. Probability inherited from Theorem 4.4 (1-2delta).

symbols.eta_W_tilde: fraction of samples from concrete heterogeneous set tilde W

tuning: alpha_r, alpha_w set at the ends of their ranges

symbols.N_cluster: total number of samples of users in the test user's true cluster

conditions: dataset completely delta-sufficient: N_u >= max{16/tilde lambda_a^2 log(8dU/(tilde lambda_a^2 delta)), 512 d/(gamma^2 tilde lambda_a) log(2U/delta)} for every user

source.label: th1
source.quote: For any $\delta \in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, assume $\mathcal{D}$ is completely $\delta$-sufficient. Then for $\alpha = 1$, $\lambda > 0$, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, the suboptimality gap satisfies SubOpt(u_test, Off-CLUB, A_test) <= \tilde{O}( sqrt(d/(tilde lambda_a N_{V(j_{u_test})})) ).

symbols.N_cluster: total number of samples of users in the test user's true cluster

source.label: th4
source.quote: If the dataset satisfies $N_{u_{\textnormal{test}}}\geq 8d$, the following lower bound holds: \inf_{\pi} \sup_{\mathcal{Q}\in\mathcal{I}_{u_{\textnormal{test}}}} \mathbb{E}[\textnormal{SubOpt}_{\mathcal{Q}}(u_{\textnormal{test}},\pi,\mathcal{A}_{\textnormal{test}})] \geq \sqrt{8d/N_{\mathcal{V}(j_{u_{\textnormal{test}}})}}.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound obtained from Theorem 2 of Li et al. (2022).
